sections.heading: C2 — Marking and signal confusables
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Marking and signal confusables with knowledge-graph hints

FACT_ID: sec11-R01 | anchor: A45
White paint always parts travelers bound the same way, while any yellow center line always splits opposing streams, so color alone names the traffic bargain. [A45]
Why it matters: group_hint color-roles; prereq_hint sec11-F02; difficulty_hint 1; confusable_with sec11-F02, sec11-F04.
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0045]
FACT_ID: sec11-R02 | anchor: A45
Dashed white waves lane changers across when clear, but solid white locks them in their lane short of special cause, one dash deciding freedom. [A45]
Why it matters: group_hint white-dash; prereq_hint sec11-F03; difficulty_hint 1; confusable_with sec11-F03.
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0045]
FACT_ID: sec11-R03 | anchor: A45
A lone dashed yellow middle invites passing between single opposing lanes, while solid yellow middles forbid it except for left turns to local doors, so the dash, not the color, grants passage. [A45]
Why it matters: group_hint yellow-dash; prereq_hint sec11-F04; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec11-F04, sec11-F06.
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0045]
FACT_ID: sec11-R04 | anchor: A46
Mixed yellow centers split permission by side, broken-side drivers passing while solid-side drivers hold, unlike twin solid stripes that bind both sides to left-turn crossings only. [A46]
Why it matters: group_hint center-combos; prereq_hint sec11-F05; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec11-F05, sec11-F06.
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0046]
FACT_ID: sec11-R05 | anchor: A46
Shared center lanes are reserved for left turns and permitted U-turns by traffic from both directions—though some become reversible lanes during rush hours—whereas reversible lanes carry traffic one way at certain times and the opposite way at other times under lane-control signs and lights [A46].
Why it matters: group_hint middle-lanes; prereq_hint sec11-F09; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec11-F09, sec11-F10.
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0046]
FACT_ID: sec11-R06 | anchor: A46
Stop lines mark where your vehicle must stop before reaching the line for a sign or signal, while crosswalks define where pedestrians cross and require yielding to pedestrians in or about to enter them, including unmarked crosswalks at intersections [A46].
Why it matters: group_hint stop-vs-walk; prereq_hint sec11-F07; difficulty_hint 1; confusable_with sec11-F07.
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0046]
FACT_ID: sec11-R07 | anchor: A46
Diamond lanes exclude all but their named riders, buses, bikes, or counted carpools, while a sharrow’s chevrons merely warn that bikes may share an open lane. [A46]
Why it matters: group_hint exclusive-vs-shared; prereq_hint sec11-F08; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec11-F08, sec11-F11.
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0046]
FACT_ID: sec11-R08 | anchor: A47
Steady lamps command absolutely, red halting and yellow warning of red, while blinking red softens to stop-sign duty and blinking yellow to mere caution. [A47]
Why it matters: group_hint steady-vs-flash; prereq_hint sec11-F12; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec11-F12, sec11-F13, sec11-F15.
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0047]
FACT_ID: sec11-R09 | anchor: A47
Red arrows jail one heading until green frees it, yellow arrows warn the green shelter is collapsing, and green arrows alone promise a defended turn. [A47]
Why it matters: group_hint arrow-trio; prereq_hint sec11-F16; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec11-F16.
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0047]
FACT_ID: sec11-R10 | anchor: A47
At a HAWK signal, solid red means pedestrians are in the crosswalk and motorists must stop, whereas flashing red means the signal is about to deactivate and drivers must stop but may proceed once pedestrians have cleared the crosswalk [A47].
Why it matters: group_hint hawk-reds; prereq_hint sec11-F18; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec11-F18, sec11-F15.
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0047]
